1.text:
Scenario 1: a new feature is added to the variability model of one domain (concrete instances 1.1-A to 1.4-A of EvolutionScenarios/concrete_scenarios.tex).



Each test performs the evolution steps up to the point where the inconsistency would arise and checks that the consistency preservation rules resolve it: the Feature CPRs create or map the realisation of the new feature in the role's model, the overlap CPRs propagate to overlapping artefacts of other roles, the reverse Feature CPRs represent new artefacts in the problem space, and the ConfigCPRs add the feature to all configurations (not selected). Whether a configuration is still a valid product is not checked here (VitruvOCL).

2.text:
Scenario 2: a new constraint is added to the variability model of one domain (concrete instances 2.1-A to 2.1-H). Expected: the configurations that are no longer valid products are detected.



Not executable in the VSUM yet: cross-tree constraints cannot be expressed with the provided UVL metamodel (no feature references in Reference / TermReference). They will be added as VitruvOCL constraints, which will check the configurations against them. The tests document the instances (data and expected outcome in the Javadoc); the expected results were checked against the three configurations with the Python twin of the check in karaceing-generator.
2.disabled: Cross-tree constraints cannot be expressed with the provided UVL metamodel (no feature references in Reference / TermReference); they will be added as VitruvOCL constraints

3.text: Scenario 3: a new solution-space artefact is added in one domain (concrete instances 3.1-A to 3.4-B). The reverse Feature CPRs ask whether the new artefact is represented by a new feature, mapped to an existing feature, or kept as a realisation detail; the overlap CPRs propagate the new artefact to the overlapping artefacts of other domains; the ConfigCPRs add new features to all configurations.

4.text: Scenario 4: a feature is removed in the problem space of one domain (concrete instances 4.1-A to 4.4-B). The Feature CPRs for removed features ask what happens with the realising artefacts (delete, keep and re-map to the parent feature, keep without feature); the overlap CPRs propagate deletions to overlapping artefacts and the BOM; the ConfigCPRs remove the feature from all configurations.

5.text:
Scenario 5: a constraint is removed from the variability model of one domain (concrete instances 5.1-A to 5.1-G). Expected: configurations that were invalid because of the constraint become valid.



Not executable in the VSUM yet: cross-tree constraints cannot be expressed with the provided UVL metamodel (no feature references in Reference / TermReference). They will be added as VitruvOCL constraints, which will check the configurations against them. The tests document the instances (data and expected outcome in the Javadoc); the expected results were checked against the three configurations with the Python twin of the check in karaceing-generator.
5.disabled: Cross-tree constraints cannot be expressed with the provided UVL metamodel (no feature references in Reference / TermReference); they will be added as VitruvOCL constraints

6.text: Scenario 6: a solution-space artefact is removed from one domain (concrete instances 6.1-A to 6.4-A). The reverse Feature CPRs remove the trace links of the removed artefact and ask whether a feature without any remaining realisation is removed; the overlap CPRs ask whether overlapping artefacts of other domains (and BOM items) are removed as well; requirement traces are cleaned up.

7.text:
The KA-RaceIng scenarios of the Inconsistency Scenarios TechReport (KA-RaceIng-1 to KA-RaceIng-10), executed as the "proposed consistency preservation" on the initial state. Each test performs the stakeholder steps of the report on the models of the VSUM and checks what Vitruvius does in between: the values propagated over the semantic overlaps (rules AR1-AR13 in KARaceIngOverlapRules, overlap kinds K1-K11 in docs/OVERLAP_CATALOGUE.md) and the notifications to the stakeholder roles (the messages "[Notify → role]").



Report artefacts are mapped onto the models of the VSUM: Brake Specification Model = des.brakesystem, SysML architecture / electrical design = elec.electrical, supplier data and procurement data = BOM item parameters, wear data = brake specification attributes. The Wiki model, performance analysis reports and the inventory model are not part of the VSUM: steps on them are documented, not executed.

scenarios.title: Brake disc becomes vented (KA-RaceIng-1)
scenarios.text: The project goals dictate weight saving, so the Project Manager adds the requirement that brake discs must be vented (step 1) and records it in the brake specification. Vitruvius updates the BOM (vented discs must be ordered, Procurement Manager) and notifies the Design Engineer that the CAD disc has no ventilation holes (not automatically resolvable, steps 2-3). The Design Engineer adds the holes (step 4); Vitruvius derives mass, inertia and heat capacity from the geometry and propagates them to the brake model of the simulation and to the BOM, and informs the Simulation, Kinematics (mass difference), Aerodynamics (notification only), Thermodynamics and Validation Engineers (step 5). The simulation no longer assumes a solid disc.

scenarios.title: Design change in the brake caliper (KA-RaceIng-2)
scenarios.text: The Project Manager adds the requirement that the calipers become two-piece (step 1); Vitruvius informs the Design Engineer about the new requirement traced to the caliper (step 2). The Design Engineer replaces the monobloc housing by two halves and moves the mounting bracket (step 3). Vitruvius creates BOM items for the halves, deletes the item of the old housing and marks the caliper as two-piece in the BOM (step 4), propagates the changed mounting interface to the electrical design (step 5), and informs the Validation Engineer (step 8) and the owner of the brake specification. The Electrical Engineer reviews the sensor and changes its part number, which Vitruvius writes to the BOM (steps 6-7).

Vitruvius propagates supplier and material (material data sheet) to the thermal model of the piston, marks the thermal analysis as outdated (step 2), updates the CAD material and informs the Validation Engineer that new pistons have to be integrated in the test bench (step 5). The Thermodynamics Engineer reruns the analysis and lowers the temperature limit (step 3); Vitruvius updates the expected result of the validation test and informs the Validation Engineer (step 4).

scenarios.title: Integration of ABS and brake over-travel switch (KA-RaceIng-6)
scenarios.text: The Project Manager decides to integrate the ABS function and the BOTS into one brake system component (step 1). The Electrical Engineer adds the integrated unit with the signal interfaces of both (it realises the brake over-travel switch, so the BOTS requirements trace to it) and then removes the two separate devices (step 2). Vitruvius detects the changed structure and propagates it to the Simulink model: a block for the integrated unit with its signal parameters is created, the blocks of the separate components are deleted (steps 3-4); the Simulation Engineer is informed to adapt the control logic (step 5).

scenarios.title: Missing wear tracking (KA-RaceIng-7)
scenarios.text: After several races the maintenance team records the wear in the brake specification: worn pads with wear warning and a disc at its minimum thickness (step 1). Vitruvius propagates the degradation to the brake model of the simulation (step 2) and informs the Simulation Engineer to rerun the performance analyses (step 3) and the Project Manager about the affected maintenance planning and operational requirements (steps 4-6).

scenarios.title: Introduction of an intermediate tyre configuration (KA-RaceIng-8)
scenarios.text: The regulations permit an intermediate tyre; the Design Engineer (here: the kinematics CAD model of the wheels) introduces the configuration (step 1), which becomes a new optional feature below Wheels. Vitruvius detects the added configuration and creates a parameter set in the tyre model of the simulation, initialised from the slick and rain tyre sets (step 2); the Simulation Engineer reviews it (step 3) and the Project Manager is informed that the performance analyses for slightly wet conditions have to be reevaluated (steps 4-5).

scenarios.title: Addition of a brake over-travel monitoring sensor (KA-RaceIng-9)

Vitruvius detects the new component and propagates it with its signal interfaces to the brake model of the Simulink model (step 3); the Simulation Engineer is asked to add the warning logic (step 4). Project documentation (Wiki model, steps 5-6) is not part of the VSUM.
